A1.justification: Both PDFs describe miniCTX, file-tuning, and NTP-TOOLKIT. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–F are readable and support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent matching the work across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on miniCTX and miniF2F, context ablations, and Math2001 experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, retrieval comparisons, context-component ablations, and supplementary analyses in Appendices B and D.

M1.justification: The core file-tuning formulation is retained. v2 Section 4.1 adds an optional inference component that appends the top 20 LeanDojo-retrieved premises from imported, non-Mathlib modules to the context for GPT-4o and file-tuned models. This extends input construction without establishing a change to the underlying architecture or training objective.

E1.justification: v2 adds HepLean physics problems, SciLean scientific-computing problems, and a PFRcross scenario targeting extensive cross-file dependencies. These substantially broaden the represented domains and contextual requirements. miniF2F and the appendix Math2001 evaluations were already present in v1.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 retains the original five baseline configurations and adds retrieval-augmented GPT-4o and file-tuning comparisons, addressing an important alternative way to supply context. GPT-4o also joins the context-component ablation in Table 4, which previously evaluated only file-tuning.

E3.justification: GPT-4o evaluation changes from pass@1 in v1 Section 5.2 to eight generated proofs and pass@8 in v2 Section 4.1. The reported Prime sample changes from 87 to 85 problems and HTPI from 185 to 45. The component ablation also changes its stated test file from Rectangle.lean to PFR.ForMathlib.Entropy.Basic and expands its controls.

E4.justification: The earlier context ablation is replaced by a seven-condition study separating environment, definitions, lemma statements, proofs, and comments for two models. v2 adds cross-file dependency analysis and an analysis relating retrieved-premise length to success in Appendix D.3. The earlier Math2001 automation tests, proof/context-length analyses, and illustrative proof examples remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new pass@8 setting changes the evaluation budget, while the premise-length distribution plot describes examples rather than estimating uncertainty in model performance.

E6.justification: v1 Table 2 reports file-tuning/state-tactic averages of 31.65%/9.31%; v2 Table 3 reports 35.94%/19.53% on the revised benchmark. New results include file-tuning at 44.19% on PFRcross, falling to 16.28% with retrieved premises. Changed coverage and GPT-4o's pass@8 protocol prevent interpreting aggregate differences as same-setting gains. miniF2F and appendix Math2001 scores are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 1 retains the same expected proof-correctness objective, and the theorem-, context-, and project-level generalization definitions are unchanged. The Lean proof examples are retained; no substantive theoretical result, derivation, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The benchmark, toolkit, and file-tuning contributions remain. However, v2 drops the abstract's claim of a new miniF2F state of the art for 1.3B models and foregrounds context benefits for both prompting and fine-tuning, together with miniF2F's inability to capture those benefits. This refines the advertised findings.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes unchanged accuracy after removing preceding proofs in its Rectangle.lean ablation; v2 interprets its different-file ablation as evidence of learning proof strategies and discusses model-dependent benefits from comments. v2 also replaces a largely prospective discussion of cross-file context with observed retrieval limitations and a proposed interference mechanism when retrieved premises dominate the prompt.

D1.justification: v2 documents selection criteria, additional premise/import metadata, a 2023 training snapshot, and more specific extraction and Lean-version instructions. Conversely, it omits v1's three training epochs, validation interval of 4,000 steps, search budgets S=32 and T=100, and several direct artifact links. These substantially change reproducibility information without establishing that the omitted settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around premise selection and existing contextual datasets, adding a benchmark-feature comparison and discussion of Graph2Tac, Magnushammer, and DeepMath. It more explicitly acknowledges prior contextual proving methods and locates miniCTX's distinction in richer context, multiple sources, and temporal evaluation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and benchmark narrative are extensively rewritten. NTP-TOOLKIT moves into the benchmark section, the standalone file-tuning exposition becomes part of the baseline descriptions, and discussion becomes a separate section. The introduction gains an explicit contribution structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds a benchmark-comparison table, a temporal-update diagram, and new dependency and premise-length plots. Dataset and performance tables gain columns and rows, and the ablation becomes a component matrix. The earlier main-text dependency chart is redrawn and moved to Appendix D.2; other retained charts are also restyled.

improvement.justification: The cross-file cases and actual retrieval comparisons address an important gap in v1 between its repository-level framework and experiments focused on preceding-file context. Expanded ablations and failure analysis provide substantially stronger evidence about useful context and retrieval limitations. These gains outweigh the loss of training/search details and the new inconsistency between 376 theorems in the text and 384 in Table 2. The assessment rests on stronger validation, rather than higher scores under changed settings.
